description: The near-infrared (NIR) camera on Clementine imaged the Moon through narrow-band filters during the mission's systematic lunar mapping. The NJM curves cover its filters at 1100, 1250, 1500, 2000 and 2600 nm.
facility_description: The Deep Space Program Science Experiment (DSPSE), better known as Clementine, was a joint mission of the US Ballistic Missile Defense Organization and NASA that tested sensors and spacecraft components in space and systematically mapped the Moon in 1994.
notes: Researched 2026-10-26. Clementine data are archived in the NASA Planetary Data System; the NASA science data licence page states there are no restrictions on usage. Design: Priest et al. (1995). Mission overview: Nozette et al. (1994). Manager review: detector part numbers and optical details not found in the linked pages were removed; DetectorType is unchanged.

licence.terms: "There are no restrictions on the usage of these data."
